chunks: And by this chain, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Abu al-Hasan al-Mawsili, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

A rabbi from the rabbis came to the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) and said, 'O Commander of the Faithful, when was your Lord?' So he said to him: 'May your mother be bereft of you! And when was He not, that it could be said when He was? My Lord was before the before, without there being a before; and after the after, without there being an after. There is neither an end-point nor a termination to His end-point — the end-points are cut off before Him, thus He is the termination of every end-point.'
Then he said, 'O Commander of the Faithful, are you then a prophet?' He said: 'Woe to you! I am but a servant among the servants of Muhammad (may God's blessings be upon him and his family).'

And it is reported that he (peace be upon him) was asked: 'Where was our Lord before He created the sky and earth?' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'Where is a question about a place, yet God was and there was no place.'

key_terms.أَيْنَ سُؤَالٌ عَنْ مَكَانٍ: 'Where' is a question about place — rejecting spatial categories for God
key_terms.الْغَايَاتُ: End-points/limits — spatial and temporal boundaries that terminate at God
key_terms.بَعْدَ الْبَعْدِ بِلَا بَعْدٍ: After the after without an after — God's post-eternal existence beyond temporal limits
key_terms.قَبْلَ الْقَبْلِ بِلَا قَبْلٍ: Before the before without a before — a statement of God's pre-eternal existence beyond temporal categories

ai.seo_question: What did Imam Ali say about when and where God existed?
ai.summary: This hadith records two profound theological exchanges involving Imam Ali (peace be upon him), transmitted via the Imam al-Sadiq (AS). In the first, a Jewish rabbi poses the question of when God 'began to exist,' and the Imam responds with the transcendent teaching that God exists before all 'befores' and after all 'afters' — beyond temporal categories entirely. In the second, he is asked where God was before creation, to which he responds that 'where' is a locational category that cannot apply to God, who existed before space itself. These exchanges reflect the Shia tradition's emphasis on divine transcendence (tanzih), where God cannot be subjected to the categories of time or space.

en.hubeali:
And by this chain, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Abu Nasr, from Abu Al Hassan Al Nowsaly,
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘A Rabbi from the Rabbis came over to Amir Al-Momineenasws and he said, ‘O Amir Al-Momineenasws! When was yourasws Lordazwj (from)?’ So heasws said to him: ‘May your mother be bereft of you! And when did Heazwj not happen to be until it can be said when myasws Lordazwj was (from). Myasws Lordazwj was before the ‘before’ without there being a ‘before’, and (will be) after the ‘after’ without there being an ‘after’. And there is neither an end-point nor a termination to Hisazwj end-point cutting off the end-point in Hisazwj Presence. Thus, Heazwj is the termination of every end-point’.
So he said, ‘O Amir Al-Momineenasws! So, are youasws a Prophetas?’ So heasws said: ‘Woe be unto you! But rather, Iasws am a servant from the servants of Muhammadsaww’.

And it is reported that he<sup>asws</sup> was asked, ‘Where was our Lord<sup>azwj</sup> before He<sup>azwj</sup> Created the sky and earth? (meaning the universe)’. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Where is a question about a place, and Allah<sup>azwj</sup> was, and there was no place’.
en.sarwar: 5. It is narrated, through the same chain of narrators and source, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid from his father from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abu Nasr from abu al-Hassan al-Muwsali from Imam abu ‘Abdallah (a.s.), who has said the following. “One of the Jewish rabbis (hibr) came to Imam Ali (a.s.), and asked, ‘O Amir al-Mu’minin, when did your Lord come into existence?’”

Imam Ali (a.s.) replied, “Bereft of you be your mother! When has Allah not been (in existence), so that it could be said when did He come into existence. My Lord existed before any before without being before. He is after every after, without being after. There is no finale destination or end for Him. All ends fall short before Him. He is the final destination of all goals.”
He further asked, “O Amir al-Mu’minin, are you a prophet?” Imam Ali (a.s.) replied, “Hold it there. I am one of the slaves of Muhammad,(s.a.) the Messenger of Allah.”

It has also been narrated that someone asked Imam Ali (a.s.) this. “Where was our Lord before the creation of the heavens and the earth?” Imam Ali (a.s.) replied, “Where is a question about space. Allah has been there before there was space.”
